ECE 6390 / Digital signals

Adaptive MODCOD

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how a transmitter trades data rate for robustness as the channel fades.

Each modulation-and-coding mode combines an alphabet size M, code rate Rc, and required quality for a stated error target. At a fixed symbol rate, information rate is Rs log₂M Rc before additional overhead.

The demonstration selects the fastest supplied mode whose toy C/N threshold is met. As a fade deepens, it can move to fewer bits per symbol or a lower code rate to preserve the stated feasibility rule.

Real switching decisions also depend on measured error performance, estimator uncertainty, feedback delay, and hysteresis. The supplied threshold table illustrates the decision mechanism rather than specifying a communication standard.

Example

At 1 Mbaud, QPSK with Rc = 1/2 carries 1 Mbit/s, while 16-QAM with Rc = 3/4 carries 3 Mbit/s before overhead.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. Why might an adaptive link delay switching upward even when a noisy C/N estimate briefly crosses a mode's nominal threshold?

    Consider prediction error, feedback delay, and rapid back-and-forth switching.

    A switching margin and hysteresis can reduce outages and unstable mode changes. A brief threshold crossing may not persist long enough to support the faster mode at its required error target.
